title: Token velocity & grace-window interaction proposal and backlog grooming
content:
Purpose:
- Capture a UX proposal for surfacing token velocity, short burst "grace windows", and per-key / per-route breakdowns in the Console.
- Produce a small backlog for engineering and experiment flags.
- Align on acceptance criteria and support playbook for burst-related incidents.

Context and problem statement:
- Customers want more actionable signals when they hit throttles or consume quotas rapidly. Current console shows aggregate rate-limit events and per-key totals, but lacks:
  - fast-moving velocity visualization (short windows),
  - an explicit notion of a short "grace" allowance that permits brief bursts without hard-blocking, and
  - route-level hotspots within a key so teams can triage which endpoints are causing bursts.
- Goal: reduce support noise and give product/infra teams tools to tune rate policies without deep log dives.

Key UX concepts proposed (high level):
1) Token velocity bands
  - Show per-key token velocity as a stacked band chart with selectable windows: 10s, 60s, 5m, 1h.
  - Band colors map to policy thresholds: green (<= baseline), amber (near soft-threshold), red (hard throttle).
  - Hover timeline shows exact tokens/sec and contributing routes.

2) Grace window indicator
  - Visual affordance that shows whether a key currently has an active grace window.
  - Grace behavior: small burst credit that decays linearly over N seconds (configurable by admins).
  - UI: a compact badge on the key card "Grace: 18s left, 120 tokens" with tooltip explaining fallback behavior.

3) Per-route heat matrix (Key x Route)
  - Sparklines or microbars for top 20 routes for a selected key, sortable by recent velocity, error-rate, and cost.
  - Clicking a route drills into a timeline with request samples, typical payload size, and example prompts (if available and permitted).

4) Simulation and "What if" slider
  - Allow operators to simulate adding load from a given route or key to see when soft/hard limits trigger.
  - Helpful for tuning autoscaling, grace duration, and queueing policy.

5) Alerting & runbook integration
  - From any throttle event card, a one-click "Create runbook" template prefilled with key, route, recent velocity, and diagnostic links.
  - Support engineer checklist: check grace state, check route hotspots, escalate to infra if >3 sustained hard-throttle windows in 1h.

Wireframe writeup (interaction flow):
- Landing: Keys table (columns: key name, tier, 1m avg tokens/s, 1h spend, active grace, recent throttles). Click a key -> opens key detail pane.
- Key detail pane top: big velocity bands over chosen time range + summary numbers (peak 1m, avg 1m, 95p latency).
- Middle: "Active policies" row (soft limit, hard limit, grace duration, burst credit). Each editable inline for admin roles (edit opens small modal).
- Bottom left: Per-route heat matrix for top 20 routes. Bottom right: Event timeline (throttle events, grace activations, autoscaler events).
- Right rail: quick actions (simulate load, create alert, mute key temporarily, export debug bundle).

Data model / telemetry needs (engineering notes):
- Short-window aggregation: ingest and retain rolling counters at 10s granularity for last 24h, 60s for 7d, 5m for 90d.
- Per-request tagging: route id, credential id, token_count, latency, outcome.
- Grace window state: server must emit events when grace opens/closes with reason and remaining credit.
- Sampling: store sampled request payloads (scrubbed) for routes flagged as problematic for quick triage.

Backlog grooming (tickets and priority):
- INF-789 (P0): short-window aggregator pipeline (10s rollups + API surface). Blocker for velocity bands.
- INF-792 (P0): grace-window state event API + storage and RFC on default durations.
- INF-801 (P1): key summary card design -> dev + QA, includes inline edit for soft/hard limits.
- INF-810 (P1): per-route heat-matrix component + route drill modal.
- INF-834 (P2): simulate-load sandbox UI and safety constraints.
- INF-840 (P2): one-click runbook template integration and export bundling.

Acceptance criteria (minimal):
- Velocity bands render for a key with 10s and 60s windows and match raw telemetry within 5% on test harness.
- Grace badge appears when server emits grace open event; countdown accurately reflects remaining credit.
- Per-route matrix shows top 20 routes ordered by 1m token velocity and clicking a route opens drill modal with last 50 sampled requests.
- Simulation tool reports threshold crossing times and does not execute real traffic.

Support/playbook excerpt (for CS and SRE):
1) Customer calls with repeated 429s: check key detail -> event timeline -> is grace opening and closing?
2) If grace used repeatedly: propose policy change: increase grace duration or add route-specific exception.
3) If hard-throttle triggered for multiple keys in same tier: investigate quota config sync issues and autoscaler logs.
4) If high velocity from single route: recommend payload-level batching, response caching, or route-specific quantization suggestions.

Open questions & decisions needed:
- Default grace model: fixed token credit vs dynamic credit proportional to historical baseline? (Pros/cons to discuss with infra team).
- Security and privacy: how much request sampling is allowed in UI; opt-in per-customer?
- UX complexity: show grace in overview table vs only in key detail (tradeoff of noise vs discoverability).

Next steps (immediate):
- Design: Leah to produce high-fidelity mock for key detail pane (due 2024-11-20).
- Eng: infra to scope INF-789 and INF-792 (due 2024-11-12).
- PM: schedule a 30m sync with SRE and CS to align runbook triggers (week of 2024-11-18).

Notes and references:
- Related ideas: "token-buckets visualizer" brainstorm in previous doc (see linked confluence).
- Customer signals: CS reported three enterprise customers asked for per-route throttling insights in the last quarter.

Rough sketches (text):
- Key row example: [redacted-key-123] | Tier: Gold | 1m: 420 t/s (▲) | 1h spend: $12.30 | Grace: 22s
- Heat matrix row: POST /v1/chat.generate ||||||| (red)  1m: 320 t/s

Appendix: short glossary
- Grace window: temporary allowance beyond soft limit for short bursts.
- Soft limit: policy threshold that triggers warnings/alerts but doesn't immediately hard-block.
- Hard throttle: immediate request rejection; visible as 429/71x in the timeline.

Feedback requested from this doc:
- Product: is grace-window a feature we want as a first-class policy? Tradeoffs?
- SRE: feasibility and suggested default backends for storing 10s rollups.
- CS: runbook template content — what fields are must-have vs nice-to-have?
_note: Generated as an internal Drive doc: mix of UX, wireframe narrative, data model notes, and backlog items. Avoids duplicating existing console rollouts docs by centering on 'grace window' concept and short-window velocity visualizations.
